subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let F := Covector (Euclid P) n (continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P with the operator norm ‖·‖), and let N := covectorEuclideanNorm, i.e. N(α) = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} for the standard orthonormal basis (e_j) of ℝ^P. Then (i) N(α + α') ≤ N(α) + N(α') for all α, α' ∈ F; (ii) N(t·α) = |t|·N(α) for all t ∈ ℝ and α ∈ F; (iii) there is a real C ≥ 0 with N(α) ≤ C·‖α‖ for all α ∈ F; and (iv) N : F → ℝ is continuous.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 2 of the supplied proof. Step 1 tests M(X) on the rescaled forms ±ω/(‖ω‖ + ε), which needs |tα| = |t||α|. Step 2 uses that 'the Euclidean coefficient norm is bounded by a constant C(P, n') times the operator norm'. See Simon Ch. 6, (1.15) and Remark 2.6. This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.mass_eq_weight-a1.test_form_approx-a1.norm_props-a1, status accepted, candidate commit f492ba4a003c8f1324077e050d48667ae23c7100), reused with its byte-identical frozen type; the proof below is the one formalized there.

Notation. e_j := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ j (j ∈ Fin P) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P, so ‖e_j‖ = 1. 𝓙 is the finite type of all maps I : Fin n → Fin P. For I ∈ 𝓙 put e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}). F carries the operator norm ‖·‖ of continuous alternating maps. By definition N(α) = √(Σ_{I∈𝓙} q_I(α)), where q_I(α) := α(e_I)² if I is strictly increasing and q_I(α) := 0 otherwise.

1. (Coefficient vector.) For α ∈ F and I ∈ 𝓙 put c_I(α) := α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing and c_I(α) := 0 otherwise. Then q_I(α) = c_I(α)² for every I. Let v(α) ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙 be the vector with coordinates c_I(α). By EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, N(α) = ‖v(α)‖ for every α. (∗)
2. (Linearity of v.) Evaluation at a fixed tuple is linear in the form, so c_I(α + α') = c_I(α) + c_I(α') and c_I(tα) = t·c_I(α) for every I. Hence v(α + α') = v(α) + v(α') and v(tα) = t·v(α).
3. (Proof of (i).) By (∗), step 2 and the triangle inequality in EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙: N(α + α') = ‖v(α) + v(α')‖ ≤ ‖v(α)‖ + ‖v(α')‖ = N(α) + N(α').
4. (Proof of (ii).) N(tα) = ‖t·v(α)‖ = |t|·‖v(α)‖ = |t|·N(α).
5. (Coordinate bound.) For every I, |c_I(α)| ≤ ‖α‖. If I is strictly increasing, the operator-norm bound for continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm) gives |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_k ‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖. Otherwise c_I(α) = 0.
6. (Proof of (iii).) Put C := √(#𝓙) ≥ 0. By step 5, Σ_I c_I(α)² ≤ #𝓙·‖α‖², so N(α) ≤ √(#𝓙·‖α‖²) = C·‖α‖.
7. (Proof of (iv).) By (i) and N(−β) = N(β) (SimonGMT covectorEuclideanNorm_neg): N(α) ≤ N(α − α') + N(α') and N(α') ≤ N(α' − α) + N(α) = N(α − α') + N(α). Hence |N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α'), which by (iii) is ≤ C·‖α − α'‖. So N is C-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul), hence continuous.
Steps 3, 4, 6 and 7 prove (i)–(iv), with C = √(Fintype.card (Fin n → Fin P)) in (iii). ∎
proof_key_steps: Write N(α) = ‖v(α)‖ for the coefficient vector v(α) = (α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing, else 0)_I in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P).
v is additive and ℝ-homogeneous; (i) and (ii) follow from the triangle inequality and homogeneity of the Euclidean norm.
|α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖, so N(α) ≤ √(card(Fin n → Fin P))·‖α‖, which is (iii).
|N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α') ≤ C‖α − α'‖, so N is Lipschitz and hence continuous, which is (iv).

That is, there is a compact K ⊆ U containing tsupport ω_j for every j such that every iterated derivative of ω_j converges uniformly on K to that of 0. Then there is a compact C ⊆ U such that ω_j(x) = 0 for every j and every x ∉ C. Moreover, for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large j, ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for every x ∈ ℝ^P, where ‖·‖ is the operator norm on n-covectors.

Source: step 2 of the supplied proof: 'if ω_j → 0 in the test-form topology (supports in one compact set, all iterated derivatives → 0 uniformly), then sup_x of the operator norm of ω_j(x) tends to 0'. This is the topology of 𝒟ⁿ(U) described before Simon 6.2.1, used with derivative order 0. This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.dpf_pfc_testFormOnConverges_zero_uniform (DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.pushforward_current-a1.uniform_small-a1, status accepted, candidate commit 8d68dfd93a5a51671384c6648f0ebabf56bd95bd), reused with its byte-identical frozen type; the proof below is the one formalized there. Notation: ω_j(x) := (ωs j : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x; ‖·‖ is the operator norm on Covector (Euclid P) n.
1. (Unfolding.) By definition of TestFormOnConverges ωs 0 there is a compact C ⊆ U with tsupport ω_j ⊆ C for every j. Moreover, for every k ∈ ℕ, iteratedFDeriv ℝ k ω_j → iteratedFDeriv ℝ k 0 uniformly on C as j → ∞. Take this C; it gives the first two conjuncts (IsCompact C and C ⊆ U).
2. (Vanishing off C.) If x ∉ C then x ∉ tsupport ω_j, so ω_j(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). This is the third conjunct.
3. (The case k = 0.) The zero test form coerces to the zero form, so iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0 x = 0. Let ε > 0. Since ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f x‖ = ‖f(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), ‖ω_j(x)‖ < ε ≤ ε there.
4. (Points off C.) For j ≥ j₀ and x ∉ C, step 2 gives ‖ω_j(x)‖ = 0 ≤ ε.
5. (Conclusion.) For every ε > 0, for all sufficiently large j, ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for every x. With steps 1–2, C satisfies all four conjuncts. ∎

k = 0 and ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f x‖ = ‖f x‖ give, eventually, ‖ω_j(x)‖ < ε on C.
Combine: eventually ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for all x.

The selected statement uses U = ℝ^P (univ, open) and n = k + 1. See Simon Ch. 6, 2.4 and 2.11. This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.cmcdt_ims_series_current (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.deformation_theorem-a1.im_series-a1.series_current-a1, status accepted, candidate commit 9e9baeffcaf4d1c42b6580605c0b8faa1afb6450), reused with its byte-identical frozen type; the proof below is the one formalized there. It uses the siblings norm_props and uniform_small.

Notation. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α (Euclidean coefficient norm); ‖α‖ is the operator norm. For Z ∈ 𝒟_n(U), M(Z) = Z.mass = M_U(Z) = sup{ofReal(Z(ω)) : ω admissible}. Here ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is admissible if |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x; tsupport ω ⊆ U holds for every test form in U. Write M(Z)^ℝ := M(Z).toReal.

1. (Norm facts; sibling norm_props.) |tα| = |t||α| for t ∈ ℝ; there is C ≥ 0 with |α| ≤ C‖α‖ for every covector α; and α ↦ |α| is continuous.
2. (Bounded coefficient norm.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). The function x ↦ |ω(x)| is continuous: ω is C^∞, hence continuous, and step 1 applies. It vanishes outside the compact set tsupport ω, since |0| = 0. So it is bounded; choose c_ω > 0 with |ω(x)| ≤ c_ω for all x.
3. (Evaluation bound.) Let Z ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with M(Z) < ∞, ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and c > 0 with |ω(x)| ≤ c for all x. Then |Z(ω)| ≤ c·M(Z)^ℝ. Indeed, for s = c⁻¹ and s = −c⁻¹ the form sω lies in 𝒟ⁿ(U), and |sω(x)| = c⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ 1 by step 1. So sω is admissible and ofReal(Z(sω)) ≤ M(Z) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn). Since M(Z) < ∞, this means s·Z(ω) = Z(sω) ≤ M(Z)^ℝ. Multiplying the two inequalities by c > 0 gives ±Z(ω) ≤ c·M(Z)^ℝ.
4. (Absolute summability.) Put A := Σ_r M(X_r) < ∞. Every M(X_r) is finite (ENNReal.ne_top_of_tsum_ne_top). The real sequence (M(X_r)^ℝ) is summable (ENNReal.summable_toReal) with Σ_r M(X_r)^ℝ = A^ℝ (ENNReal.tsum_toReal_eq). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), steps 2–3 give |X_r(ω)| ≤ c_ω·M(X_r)^ℝ for every r. So Σ_r |X_r(ω)| < ∞, and the real series Σ_r X_r(ω) is summable (Summable.of_norm_bounded).
5. (Linear functional.) Put L(ω) := Σ_r X_r(ω). Since each X_r is linear and the series are summable, L(ω + ω') = L(ω) + L(ω') (Summable.tsum_add) and L(tω) = t·L(ω) (tsum_mul_left).
6. (Uniform bound.) If c > 0 and |ω(x)| ≤ c for all x, then |L(ω)| ≤ Σ_r |X_r(ω)| ≤ Σ_r c·M(X_r)^ℝ = c·A^ℝ. This uses norm_tsum_le_tsum_norm, Summable.tsum_le_tsum and step 3.
7. (Continuity.) First, A^ℝ ≥ 0: apply step 6 to ω = 0 and c = 1, using L(0) = 0. Let ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U), i.e. TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0. Let η > 0 and put ε := η/(2(C + 1)(A^ℝ + 1)) > 0. By sibling uniform_small, for all large j, ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for every x. Then |ω_j(x)| ≤ C‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ Cε ≤ (C + 1)ε. Step 6 with c := (C + 1)ε gives |L(ω_j)| ≤ (C + 1)ε·A^ℝ ≤ (C + 1)ε(A^ℝ + 1) = η/2 < η. Hence L(ω_j) → 0. This is the continuity condition of GeometricCurrentOn, so there is Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with Y(ω) = L(ω) for every ω. By step 4, HasSum (r ↦ X_r(ω)) (Y(ω)) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); this is conclusion (i).
8. (Mass.) Let ω be admissible. The terms max(X_r(ω), 0) are nonnegative and bounded by |X_r(ω)|, so they are summable; also X_r(ω) ≤ max(X_r(ω), 0). Hence Y(ω) = Σ_r X_r(ω) ≤ Σ_r max(X_r(ω), 0). Therefore ofReal(Y(ω)) ≤ ofReal(Σ_r max(X_r(ω), 0)) = Σ_r ofReal(max(X_r(ω), 0)) (ENNReal.ofReal_tsum_of_nonneg) = Σ_r ofReal(X_r(ω)). This is ≤ Σ_r M(X_r), because ω is admissible for every M(X_r) (le_massOn). Taking the supremum over admissible ω gives M(Y) ≤ Σ_r M(X_r); this is conclusion (ii).
9. (Support, using (VO).) Let E := closure(⋃_r spt X_r), a closed set, and let x ∈ spt Y; then x ∈ U, since spt Y ⊆ U. Suppose x ∉ E. As U is open, U ∖ E is open and contains x. Choose ε > 0 with B_ε(x) ⊆ U ∖ E and put W := B_{ε/2}(x). Then W is open, and closure W ⊆ B̄_{ε/2}(x) ⊆ B_ε(x) ⊆ U ∖ E ⊆ U. Also closure W is compact, being closed and bounded in ℝ^P. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. For each r, spt X_r ⊆ E, while tsupport ω ⊆ closure W ⊆ U ∖ E. So tsupport ω and spt X_r are disjoint, and (VO) gives X_r(ω) = 0. Hence HasSum (r ↦ X_r(ω)) 0. By uniqueness of sums in the Hausdorff space ℝ and (i), Y(ω) = 0. So Y vanishes on W, and W is one of the sets whose union is zeroRegion Y. Then x ∈ W ⊆ zeroRegion Y, contradicting x ∈ spt Y = U ∖ zeroRegion Y. Therefore spt Y ⊆ E; this is conclusion (iii). ∎
proof_key_steps: Admissibility of ±c⁻¹ω gives |Z(ω)| ≤ c·M(Z) whenever |ω(x)| ≤ c; test forms have bounded coefficient norm.
Σ_r M(X_r) < ∞ makes Σ_r X_r(ω) absolutely summable; L(ω) := Σ_r X_r(ω) is linear with |L(ω)| ≤ c·Σ_r M(X_r) when |ω| ≤ c.
Uniform smallness of test forms converging to 0 and |α| ≤ C‖α‖ make L sequentially continuous, so L is a current Y with HasSum (X_r(ω)) (Y(ω)).
For admissible ω, ofReal(Y(ω)) ≤ Σ_r ofReal(X_r(ω)) ≤ Σ_r M(X_r), so M(Y) ≤ Σ_r M(X_r).
For x ∉ closure ⋃ spt X_r, a small ball W around x has compact closure inside U ∖ closure ⋃ spt X_r; (VO) kills every X_r(ω) with tsupport ω ⊆ W, so Y vanishes on W and x ∉ spt Y.

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent planes of an IMRep carrier pass to locally finite supersets (reused accepted rsdic_imrep_ae_tangent_orient_of_subset)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep in U, and B, C ⊆ ℝ^P Borel sets with B ⊆ M, B ⊆ C ⊆ U and Hⁿ(C ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ B there is a linear subspace Q of ℝ^P such that C has approximate tangent space Q at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q) and ξ(x) is a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U B C : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet B → MeasurableSet C → B ⊆ R.carrier → B ⊆ C → C ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (C ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict B), ∃ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step (5c) of the supplied proof. By (IMC)(a) for M_i ⊆ N, the approximate tangent space Q_i(x) of M_i, oriented by ξ_i(x), is also one of N. This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.rsdic_imrep_ae_tangent_orient_of_subset (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.integer_combination-a1.imrep_tangent_transfer-a1, status accepted, candidate commit a02fee1b895fd5361bd0d6d2865e4b0d85f5d08a), reused with its byte-identical frozen type. The proof below is the one formalized there. It uses the sibling tangent_locality, i.e. the accepted Submission.rsdic_ae_tangent_iff_of_subset. Notation: μ := Hⁿ = μHE[n], M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient.
1. (M is locally finite in U.) M is Borel and M ⊆ U (fields measurableSet_carrier, carrier_subset). For compact K ⊆ U: θ is ℕ-valued and positive on M, so θ ≥ 1 on M. Hence μ(M ∩ K) = ∫_{M∩K} 1 dμ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dμ < ∞ by locallyIntegrable_mult.
2. Apply tangent_locality with open U, small set B and large set M. Here B ⊆ M ⊆ U are Borel and M is locally finite by step 1. So for μ⌞B-a.e. x and every Q: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q.
3. Apply tangent_locality with open U, small set B and large set C, using the hypotheses on B and C. So for μ⌞B-a.e. x and every Q: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q.
4. The field orients of R says: for μ⌞M-a.e. x there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. Since B ⊆ M, μ⌞B ≤ μ⌞M, so this also holds for μ⌞B-a.e. x.
5. Let x lie outside the union of the three μ⌞B-null exceptional sets of steps 2–4, and take Q from step 4. By step 2 (⟹), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q. By step 3 (⟸), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q. And IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q holds. This proves the claim for μ⌞B-a.e. x. ∎
proof_key_steps: The carrier M of an IMRep is Borel and locally Hⁿ-finite in U because θ ≥ 1 on M.
tangent_locality for B ⊆ M and for B ⊆ C: a.e. on B, the tangent spaces of B, M and C at x coincide.
The orients field of R holds a.e. on B ⊆ M; combining gives an approximate tangent space of C at x oriented by ξ(x).

subproblems.title: Two unit orientations of the same plane differ by a sign (reused accepted rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P, and v, w ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n: continuous linear functionals on n-covectors) with IsUnitOrientationOf v Q and IsUnitOrientationOf w Q. That is, each of v and w is ±(α ↦ α(τ)) for some orthonormal family τ : Fin n → ℝ^P spanning Q. Then w = v or w = −v.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (v w : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), IsUnitOrientationOf v Q → IsUnitOrientationOf w Q → w = v ∨ w = -v
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: (L3) in step (5d) of the supplied proof: two orthonormal bases of Q differ by an orthogonal matrix of determinant ±1 (cf. Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.integer_combination-a1.orientation_sign-a1, status accepted, candidate commit fe95347baaed6a2cf2ecde4455e2b32f361fde51), reused with its byte-identical frozen type; the proof below is the one formalized there.
1. (Unfolding the hypotheses.) There are orthonormal families τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P with span(range τ) = Q = span(range τ'). There are signs ε, ε' ∈ {1, −1} with v(α) = ε·α(τ) and w(α) = ε'·α(τ') for every n-covector α.
2. Each τ_i and τ'_i lies in Q, so τ and τ' are orthonormal families in the inner product space Q. Since τ is linearly independent and spans Q, dim Q = n. An orthonormal family of n vectors in the n-dimensional space Q is a basis of Q. Hence τ and τ' are orthonormal bases b and b' of Q indexed by Fin n.
3. Let d := det_b(b'), the determinant of the change-of-basis matrix from b to b'. Both bases are orthonormal, so this matrix is orthogonal and d ∈ {1, −1} (Mathlib OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real).
4. Let α be an n-covector and α_Q its restriction to Q, an alternating n-linear form on the n-dimensional space Q. Every such form is a multiple of det_b: α_Q = α_Q(b)·det_b (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). Evaluating at b' gives α(τ') = α_Q(b') = α_Q(b)·det_b(b') = d·α(τ). The number d does not depend on α.
5. Hence for every α: w(α) = ε'·α(τ') = ε'd·α(τ) = (εε'd)·(ε·α(τ)) = s·v(α), where s := εε'd ∈ {1, −1} (using ε² = 1). Therefore w = s·v, i.e. w = v if s = 1 and w = −v if s = −1. For n = 0 the same argument applies: τ = τ' is the empty family, Q = {0} and d = 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: Both orthonormal families spanning Q are orthonormal bases b, b' of Q.
det_b(b') = ±1 because the change-of-basis matrix is orthogonal.
For every n-covector α, α(τ') = det_b(b')·α(τ), since alternating n-forms on Q are multiples of det_b.
Therefore w = (εε'det_b(b'))·v with εε'det_b(b') ∈ {±1}.

subproblems.title: Locality of approximate tangent spaces (reused accepted rsdic_ae_tangent_iff_of_subset)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and A ⊆ B ⊆ U Borel sets with Hⁿ(B ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A and every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P: B has approximate tangent space Q at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q) if and only if A has approximate tangent space Q at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U A B : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → A ⊆ B → B ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (B ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict A), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: this is (IMC)(a) of the selected statement with the two sides of the equivalence swapped. It is used in (5c) and (5g) of the supplied proof. Mathematically it is Simon Ch. 3, Remarks 1.5(2) and 1.8(1), with the density theorem of Ch. 1, 3.16. This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.rsdic_ae_tangent_iff_of_subset (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.integer_combination-a1.tangent_locality-a1, status accepted, candidate commit a157a5f4f62ba1c354a3b0cc070d947560abf2e6), reused with its byte-identical frozen type. The proof below is the one formalized there, with its growth lemma (the accepted Submission.rsdic_measure_closedBall_le_of_tangent) written out in step 5. Notation: μ := Hⁿ = μHE[n]; B̄_r(z) and B_r(z) are the closed and open balls; for ρ > 0, η_ρ(y) := ρ⁻¹(y − x) (blowUpMap x ρ).
1. (Countable compact cover.) Let 𝒟 ⊆ ℝ^P be countable and dense, and 𝒥 := {(c, r) ∈ 𝒟 × ℚ : r > 0, B̄_r(c) ⊆ U}, a countable set. For j = (c, r) put K_j := B̄_r(c), a compact subset of U. Every y ∈ U lies in B_r(c) for some (c, r) ∈ 𝒥. Indeed, choose ε > 0 with B̄_ε(y) ⊆ U, c ∈ 𝒟 with |y − c| < ε/3, and rational r ∈ (ε/3, 2ε/3). Then |y − c| < r and B̄_r(c) ⊆ B̄_ε(y) ⊆ U.
2. (Density theorem.) For j ∈ 𝒥, λ_j := μ⌞(B ∩ K_j) is a finite Borel measure, since μ(B ∩ K_j) < ∞. Apply Besicovitch's density theorem (Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div) to λ_j and A. For λ_j⌞A-a.e. x, λ_j(A ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/λ_j(B̄_ρ(x)) → 1 as ρ ↓ 0. Since A ⊆ B, λ_j⌞A = μ⌞(A ∩ K_j). So there is a μ-null set N_j such that the convergence holds at every x ∈ (A ∩ K_j) ∖ N_j. Then N := ⋃_j N_j is μ-null.
3. (Local notation.) Fix x ∈ A ∖ N. Take j = (c, r) ∈ 𝒥 with x ∈ B_r(c), and δ₀ := (r − |x − c|)/2 > 0, so B̄_{δ₀}(x) ⊆ K_j. For 0 < ρ ≤ δ₀ and Z ⊆ B, λ_j(Z ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = μ(Z ∩ B̄_ρ(x)). Write a(ρ) := μ(B ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) and b(ρ) := μ(A ∩ B̄_ρ(x)). Both are finite for ρ ≤ δ₀, and b(ρ)/a(ρ) → 1.
4. (Small excess.) For each ε ∈ (0, 1) there is ρ_ε ∈ (0, δ₀] with μ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ ε·a(ρ) for 0 < ρ < ρ_ε. Indeed, choose ρ_ε with b/a > 1 − ε there. Then a(ρ) > 0 and b ≥ (1 − ε)a. Since A ⊆ B and everything is finite, μ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = a − b ≤ εa.
5. (Growth.) Suppose D ∈ {A, B} has an approximate tangent space Q at x. D is Borel and μ(D ∩ B̄_{δ₀}(x)) ≤ a(δ₀) < ∞.
   - Scaling: μ is translation invariant and μ(cW) = |c|ⁿμ(W) (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). Also η_ρ(Z) ∩ B̄_R(0) = η_ρ(Z ∩ B̄_{Rρ}(x)). Hence μ(η_ρ(Z) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = ρ^{−n} μ(Z ∩ B̄_{Rρ}(x)) for all Z and ρ, R > 0.
   - Test function: f(y) := max(0, min(1, 2 − |y|)) lies in C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ) and satisfies 1_{B̄_1(0)} ≤ f ≤ 1_{B̄_2(0)}. For 0 < ρ ≤ δ₀/2, f is integrable on η_ρ(D), and ∫_{η_ρ(D)} f dμ ≥ μ(η_ρ(D) ∩ B̄_1(0)) = ρ^{−n} μ(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x)).
   - Limit: by Definition 1.4, ∫_{η_ρ(D)} f dμ → L := ∫_Q f dμ as ρ ↓ 0. So there is r₁ > 0 with μ(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ (L + 1)ρⁿ for 0 < ρ < r₁. Put K₀ := max(L + 1, 0).
   - Case D = B: a(ρ) ≤ K₀ρⁿ for 0 < ρ < r₁.
   - Case D = A: for 0 < ρ < min(r₁, ρ_{1/2}), a(ρ) = b(ρ) + μ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ K₀ρⁿ + a(ρ)/2. Hence a(ρ) ≤ 2K₀ρⁿ.
   In both cases a(ρ) ≤ Kρⁿ for 0 < ρ < r₂, with some K ≥ 0 and r₂ > 0. With step 4 this gives (†) ρ^{−n} μ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0.
6. (Comparison of blow-ups.) Assume (†). Let g ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), R ≥ 1 with g = 0 outside B̄_R(0), and M_g := sup|g|. For 0 < ρ < δ₀/R, μ(η_ρ(B) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = ρ^{−n} a(Rρ) < ∞. So g is integrable on η_ρ(B) and on its Borel subsets η_ρ(A) and η_ρ(B ∖ A). Since η_ρ is injective, ∫_{η_ρ(B)} g − ∫_{η_ρ(A)} g = ∫_{η_ρ(B∖A)} g. Its absolute value is at most M_g ρ^{−n} μ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_{Rρ}(x)) = M_g Rⁿ (Rρ)^{−n} μ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_{Rρ}(x)), which tends to 0 by (†).
7. (Conclusion.) Let x ∈ A ∖ N and Q a subspace. If HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q, then dim Q = n, step 5 applies with D = B, and step 6 gives ∫_{η_ρ(A)} g dμ → ∫_Q g dμ for every g. Hence HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q. Conversely, step 5 with D = A and step 6 give HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q. The null set N does not depend on Q and μ⌞A(N) = 0, so the equivalence holds for μ⌞A-a.e. x and all Q simultaneously. For n = 0 the argument is unchanged. ∎
proof_key_steps: Cover U by countably many compact balls K_j ⊆ U whose interiors cover U.
Besicovitch density theorem for the finite measures Hⁿ⌞(B ∩ K_j): Hⁿ(A ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/Hⁿ(B ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) → 1 for a.e. x ∈ A.
If A or B has a tangent plane at x, the scaling and test-function argument gives Hⁿ(B ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = O(ρⁿ), so Hⁿ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = o(ρⁿ).
Then |∫_{η_ρ(B)} g − ∫_{η_ρ(A)} g| → 0 for every g ∈ C_c, so the limits in Definition 1.4 coincide.

subproblems.title: A unit orientation has operator norm at most one (reused accepted unit_orientation_norm_le_one)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P, and ξ ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n, the continuous dual of the n-covectors with the operator norm) with IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q. Then ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ξ : MultiVector P n), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the domination |ξ_i(x)(ω(x))| ≤ ‖ω‖ in step (5f) of the supplied proof, in its operator-norm form. It replaces the use of (IMC)(d) there. This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.unit_orientation_norm_le_one (DAG node root.half_space_cone_lies_in_boundary-a1.imrep_measure_unique-a1.orientation_norm_bound-a1, status accepted, candidate commit 0325970d8b47298803106a41abbcdb3c8c9ac103), reused with its byte-identical frozen type; the proof below is the one formalized there. Covectors carry the operator norm of continuous alternating maps; MultiVector P n is their continuous dual with the operator norm.
1. By IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q choose an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n). Either ξ(α) = α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for every n-covector α, or ξ(α) = −α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for every α. That τ spans Q is not used.
2. Fix α. By the multilinear operator-norm bound (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm), |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_i ‖τ_i‖. Orthonormality gives ‖τ_i‖ = 1, so the product is 1 (the empty product for n = 0). Hence |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖.
3. In either sign case, |ξ(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ 1·‖α‖.
4. Step 3 holds for every α, and 1 ≥ 0, so ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound gives ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: Unpack IsUnitOrientationOf: ξ(α) = ±α(τ) for an orthonormal family τ.
|α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏‖τ_i‖ = ‖α‖ by the multilinear operator-norm bound.
Hence |ξ(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for all α, so ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1 (opNorm_le_bound).

subproblems.title: A common Borel reference orientation for countably many IMReps (reused accepted cmcdt_ims_common_orientation)

subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : ℕ → IMRep U n), IsOpen U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] ((⋃ i, (R i).carrier) ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∃ (η : Euclid P → MultiVector P n) (s : ℕ → Euclid P → ℝ), StronglyMeasurable η ∧ (∀ i, Measurable (s i)) ∧ (∀ i x, s i x = 1 ∨ s i x = -1) ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (⋃ i, (R i).carrier)), ∃ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (⋃ i, (R i).carrier) x Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (η x) Q) ∧ ∀ i, ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (R i).carrier), (R i).orient x = s i x • η x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps (5c) and (5d) of the supplied proof, stated for an arbitrary open U and degree n. They comprise the Borel modification of the ξ_i, the common approximate tangent space Q(x) of N, the reference orientation η(x) := ξ_{ι(x)}(x) with ι(x) := min{i : x ∈ M_i}, and the signs s_i. Here (IMC)(a) combined with the orientation field is the sibling tangent_transfer, and (L3) is the sibling orientation_sign. This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.cmcdt_ims_common_orientation (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.deformation_theorem-a1.im_series-a1.common_orientation-a1, status accepted, candidate commit 417be912f27f01021b2cd189bd274b9ce74e6fb7), reused with its byte-identical frozen type; the proof below is the one formalized there.

Notation: μ := Hⁿ = μHE[n]; M_i := R_i.carrier, ξ_i := R_i.orient, N := ⋃_i M_i.

1. (Sets.) Each M_i is Borel and M_i ⊆ U (IMRep fields), so N is Borel and N ⊆ U.
2. (Borel versions.) ξ_i is a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞M_i. Let ξ'_i := AEStronglyMeasurable.mk ξ_i: ξ'_i is strongly measurable and ξ'_i = ξ_i μ-a.e. on M_i.
3. (Disjoint pieces.) D_i := M_i ∖ ⋃_{j<i} M_j (Mathlib disjointed). The D_i are Borel and pairwise disjoint, D_i ⊆ M_i, and ⋃_i D_i = N.
4. (Reference orientation.) η(x) := Σ'_i 1_{D_i}(x)·ξ'_i(x). At most one term is nonzero, so η = ξ'_j on D_j (tsum_eq_single) and η = 0 off N. For x ∈ N, x ∈ D_{ι(x)} with ι(x) = min{i : x ∈ M_i}, so η(x) = ξ'_{ι(x)}(x). To see that η is strongly measurable, define g_0 := 0 and g_{k+1}(x) := ξ'_k(x) if x ∈ D_k and g_k(x) otherwise. Each g_k is strongly measurable (piecewise definition on a Borel set). If x ∈ D_j, then g_k(x) = ξ'_j(x) = η(x) for all k > j. If x ∉ N, then g_k(x) = 0 = η(x) for all k. So g_k → η pointwise, and η is strongly measurable as a pointwise limit of strongly measurable functions into the metrizable space MultiVector P n (stronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto).
5. (Signs.) s_i(x) := 1 if ξ'_i(x) = η(x) and s_i(x) := −1 otherwise. The set {ξ'_i = η} is Borel, being the equality set of two strongly measurable maps into a metrizable space (StronglyMeasurable.measurableSet_eq_fun). So s_i is measurable and takes only the values ±1.
6. (Tangent planes along N.) Fix j. Apply tangent_transfer to R_j with B := M_j and C := N. Its hypotheses hold: M_j and N are Borel, M_j ⊆ M_j, M_j ⊆ N ⊆ U, and N is locally finite by hypothesis. So for μ-a.e. x ∈ M_j there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_j(x)) Q. Since ξ'_j = ξ_j a.e. on M_j, also IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ'_j(x)) Q a.e. on M_j. As M_j is Borel, this reads: for μ⌞N-a.e. x, x ∈ M_j implies that statement (ae_restrict_iff'). By countability (ae_all_iff), for μ⌞N-a.e. x: for every j with x ∈ M_j there is Q_j with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q_j and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ'_j(x)) Q_j. (†)
7. (Signs a.e. on N.) Let x ∈ N satisfy (†). Then x ∈ D_j for some j (step 3), hence x ∈ M_j and η(x) = ξ'_j(x). So (†) gives Q_j with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q_j and IsUnitOrientationOf (η(x)) Q_j; this is conclusion (a) at x. Let i be any index with x ∈ M_i. By (†), Q_i is also an approximate tangent space of N at x, so Q_i = Q_j (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique). Thus η(x) and ξ'_i(x) are unit orientations of the same Q_j, and orientation_sign gives ξ'_i(x) = η(x) or ξ'_i(x) = −η(x). Hence for μ⌞N-a.e. x, (a) holds and ξ'_i(x) = ±η(x) for every i with x ∈ M_i.
8. (Conclusion (b).) Fix i. Since M_i ⊆ N, μ⌞M_i-a.e. statements follow from μ⌞N-a.e. ones (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset). So for μ-a.e. x ∈ M_i both ξ_i(x) = ξ'_i(x) and ξ'_i(x) = ±η(x) hold. If ξ'_i(x) = η(x), then s_i(x) = 1 and ξ_i(x) = η(x) = 1·η(x). Otherwise ξ'_i(x) ≠ η(x), so ξ'_i(x) = −η(x) and s_i(x) = −1; then ξ_i(x) = −η(x) = (−1)·η(x) (neg_one_smul). Together with steps 4, 5 and 7, all conclusions hold. ∎
proof_key_steps: Replace each ξ_i by a strongly measurable ξ'_i equal to it a.e. on M_i, and disjointify the carriers: D_i := M_i ∖ ⋃_{j<i} M_j.
η := Σ_i 1_{D_i}ξ'_i equals ξ'_{ι(x)} on N; it is strongly measurable as the pointwise limit of ite-built approximants.
tangent_transfer for M_j ⊆ N: a.e. on N, every ξ'_j(x) with x ∈ M_j is a unit orientation of an approximate tangent space of N at x.
Uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces and orientation_sign give, a.e. on N, a tangent plane oriented by η(x) and ξ'_i(x) = ±η(x) whenever x ∈ M_i.
With the measurable signs s_i := (1 if ξ'_i = η else −1), ξ_i = s_iη a.e. on M_i.

subproblems.title: An integer-valued density on an oriented rectifiable set gives an IMRep (reused accepted cmcdt_ims_imrep_of_int_density)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P open. Let N ⊆ U be Borel and countably n-rectifiable with Hⁿ(N ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. Let η : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n) be strongly measurable. Let m : ℝ^P → ℝ be measurable with m(x) ∈ ℤ for every x and ∫_{N∩K} |m| dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. Assume that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ N there is a linear subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (η(x)) Q. Then there is an IMRep R in U such that R.action(ω) = ∫_N m(x)·η(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every n-form ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, no regularity required).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U N : Set (Euclid P)) (η : Euclid P → MultiVector P n) (m : Euclid P → ℝ), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet N → N ⊆ U → CountablyRectifiable n N → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (N ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → StronglyMeasurable η → Measurable m → (∀ x, ∃ z : ℤ, m x = z) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∫⁻ x in N ∩ K, ‖m x‖ₑ ∂μHE[n] ≠ ∞) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict N), ∃ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (η x) Q) → ∃ R : IMRep U n, ∀ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, R.action ω = ∫ x in N, m x * η x (ω x) ∂μHE[n]

Source: steps (5e) and (5g) of the supplied proof, stated for an arbitrary open U and degree n: the IMRep (N', |m|, sign(m)η) built from an integer multiplicity m and an orientation η of N. Tangent planes pass from N to N' by locality, which is (IMC)(a), here the sibling tangent_locality. The supplied proof's removal of a null set Z is unnecessary because the IMRep fields are a.e. conditions. This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.cmcdt_ims_imrep_of_int_density (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.deformation_theorem-a1.im_series-a1.density_imrep-a1, status accepted, candidate commit c48b246382e6d5141d80cb617ebabdf541a30fec), reused with its byte-identical frozen type; the proof below is the one formalized there.

Notation: μ := Hⁿ = μHE[n].

1. (Carrier.) N' := N ∩ {x : m(x) ≠ 0}. It is Borel: N is Borel and m is measurable, so {m ≠ 0} = m⁻¹(ℝ ∖ {0}) is Borel. Also N' ⊆ N ⊆ U.
2. (Multiplicity.) mult(x) := ⌊|m(x)|⌋₊ ∈ ℕ (Nat.floor). For every x, m(x) = z for some z ∈ ℤ, and |m(x)| = |z| is the natural number natAbs z, so (mult(x) : ℝ) = |m(x)|. mult is measurable as the composition of the measurable m, the continuous |·| and the monotone, hence measurable, ⌊·⌋₊ : ℝ → ℕ (Monotone.measurable). For x ∈ N', m(x) ≠ 0, so mult(x) = |m(x)| > 0.
3. (Orientation.) orient(x) := −η(x) if m(x) < 0, and orient(x) := η(x) otherwise. It is strongly measurable: η and −η = (−1)•η are strongly measurable, {m < 0} is Borel, and the piecewise combination is strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.ite). In particular orient is a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞N'.
4. (Rectifiability, local integrability.) N' ⊆ N, so N' is countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono). For compact K ⊆ U: ∫_{N'∩K} mult dμ ≤ ∫_{N∩K} mult dμ = ∫_{N∩K} |m| dμ < ∞, by monotonicity in the set, step 2 and the hypothesis.
5. (Orientation field.) Apply sibling tangent_locality with open U, small set N' and large set N. Here N' ⊆ N ⊆ U are Borel and N is locally finite by hypothesis. So for μ⌞N'-a.e. x and every Q: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N' x Q. The hypothesis on η holds μ⌞N-a.e., hence μ⌞N'-a.e., since N' ⊆ N. Take x outside both exceptional null sets and Q from the hypothesis. Then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N' x Q, and orient(x) ∈ {η(x), −η(x)} is a unit orientation of Q. Indeed, if η(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α (resp. −α(τ)), with τ orthonormal spanning Q, then −η(x)(α) = −α(τ) (resp. α(τ)); IsUnitOrientationOf allows either sign with the same τ.
6. Steps 1–5 verify every field of IMRep (measurableSet_carrier, carrier_subset, rectifiable, measurable_mult, mult_pos, locallyIntegrable_mult, aestronglyMeasurable_orient, orients). So R := (N', mult, orient) is an IMRep in U.
7. (Action.) Let ω be any n-form. For x ∈ N:
   - if m(x) = 0, then x ∉ N' and 1_{N'}(x)·mult(x)·orient(x)(ω(x)) = 0 = m(x)·η(x)(ω(x));
   - if m(x) ≠ 0, then x ∈ N' and mult(x)·orient(x)(ω(x)) = |m(x)|·(±η(x)(ω(x))) = m(x)·η(x)(ω(x)), the sign being that of m(x).
   So the functions 1_{N'}·mult·orient(ω) and m·η(ω) agree at every point of N. Hence R.action(ω) = ∫_{N'} mult·orient(ω) dμ = ∫_{N ∩ N'} mult·orient(ω) dμ (since N ∩ N' = N') = ∫_N 1_{N'}·mult·orient(ω) dμ (setIntegral_indicator) = ∫_N m·η(ω) dμ (setIntegral_congr_fun). No integrability is needed: Bochner integrals over N of functions that agree pointwise on N coincide. ∎
proof_key_steps: Carrier N' := N ∩ {m ≠ 0} (Borel), multiplicity ⌊|m|⌋₊ = |m| (measurable, positive on N'), orientation sign(m)·η (strongly measurable).
N' ⊆ N gives rectifiability; ∫_{N'∩K} |m| ≤ ∫_{N∩K} |m| < ∞ gives local integrability.
tangent_locality for N' ⊆ N moves the oriented approximate tangent planes of N to N'; ±η(x) is still a unit orientation.
1_{N'}·|m|·sign(m)η(ω) = m·η(ω) pointwise on N, so R.action(ω) = ∫_N m·η(ω) dHⁿ for every form ω.

subproblems.title: A countable family of IMReps with finite total mass is represented by one IMRep (reused accepted cmcdt_ims_imrep_tsum)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and R_i = (M_i, θ_i, ξ_i) (i ∈ ℕ) IMReps in U with Σ_i μ_{R_i}(U) < ∞, where μ_R := θ·Hⁿ⌞M is IMRep.measure. Then there is an IMRep R' in U such that for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the real series Σ_i R_i.action(ω) has sum R'.action(ω) (HasSum). Here R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : ℕ → IMRep U n), IsOpen U → ∑' i, (R i).measure U ≠ ∞ → ∃ R' : IMRep U n, ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, HasSum (fun i => (R i).action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) (R'.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n))

Source: step 5 of the supplied proof ((5a)–(5g)) at the level of IMReps, stated for an arbitrary open U and degree n. The parent applies this child to IMReps R_i of the W_i, after converting M(W_i) = μ_{R_i}(ℝ^P) by (MR). Steps (5c)–(5d) are the sibling common_orientation and step (5g) is the sibling density_imrep. The integer density is the real tsum m = Σ'_i s_iθ_i1_{M_i}, which is 0 where the series does not converge; it is integer-valued everywhere, so no exceptional set has to be removed. This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.cmcdt_ims_imrep_tsum (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.deformation_theorem-a1.im_series-a1.imrep_tsum-a1, status accepted, candidate commit c9573f9d1e1ecf9ca2594f227f83826f0f5003c4), reused with its byte-identical frozen type; the proof below is the one formalized there.

Notation: μ := Hⁿ = μHE[n]; M_i := R_i.carrier, θ_i := R_i.mult, ξ_i := R_i.orient; A := Σ_i μ_{R_i}(U) < ∞.

1. (Masses.) Θ_i := 1_{M_i}·θ_i is [0, ∞]-valued, finite and measurable. U is open, hence Borel, and M_i ⊆ U. So μ_{R_i}(U) = ∫_U θ_i d(μ⌞M_i) (withDensity_apply) = ∫_{M_i} θ_i dμ = ∫ Θ_i dμ (lintegral_indicator). Θ := Σ_i Θ_i is measurable, and ∫ Θ dμ = Σ_i ∫ Θ_i dμ = A < ∞ (lintegral_tsum).
2. (The union.) N := ⋃_i M_i is Borel, N ⊆ U, and N is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_iUnion). Also μ(N) ≤ Σ_i μ(M_i) ≤ Σ_i ∫_{M_i} θ_i dμ = A, since θ_i ≥ 1 on M_i (mult_pos) gives μ(M_i) = ∫_{M_i} 1 ≤ ∫_{M_i} θ_i. Hence μ(N ∩ K) ≤ A < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U.
3. (Common orientation.) Apply sibling common_orientation to (R_i), with U open and the bound of step 2. It gives a strongly measurable η and measurable s_i with values in {1, −1} such that: (a) for μ⌞N-a.e. x there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (η(x)) Q; (b) ξ_i = s_i·η μ-a.e. on M_i, for every i.
4. (The integer density.) a_i := 1_{M_i}·s_i·θ_i is real-valued and measurable. Since |s_i| = 1, |a_i| = Θ_i (as real numbers), and a_i(x) ∈ ℤ. Put m(x) := Σ'_i a_i(x), the real tsum, which is 0 when the series is not summable. m is measurable (Measurable.tsum).
   - m(x) ∈ ℤ for every x. If (a_i(x))_i is summable, then a_i(x) → 0 along the cofinite filter, so |a_i(x)| < 1 for all but finitely many i. For an integer this forces a_i(x) = 0 (Int.abs_lt_one_iff). So only finitely many terms are nonzero, and m(x) is a finite sum of integers (tsum_eq_sum). If the series is not summable, m(x) = 0.
   - ‖m(x)‖ₑ ≤ Σ_i ‖a_i(x)‖ₑ = Θ(x) for every x (enorm_tsum_le_tsum_enorm). Hence ∫_{N∩K} |m| dμ ≤ ∫ Θ dμ = A < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U.
5. (The IMRep.) Steps 2–4 and 3(a) are exactly the hypotheses of sibling density_imrep for (U, N, η, m). It gives an IMRep R' in U with R'.action(ω) = ∫_N m(x)·η(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every n-form ω.
6. (Dominated convergence.) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); it is continuous with compact support, so there is B ≥ 0 with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ B for all x (HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous). The map x ↦ η(x)(ω(x)) is strongly measurable: it is the image of the strongly measurable pair x ↦ (η(x), x) under the continuous map (ξ, y) ↦ ξ(ω(y)) (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply). By 3(a) and sibling orient_norm, ‖η(x)‖ ≤ 1 for μ⌞N-a.e. x, so there |η(x)(ω(x))| ≤ ‖η(x)‖·‖ω(x)‖ ≤ B. On the measure space (ℝ^P, μ⌞N) put F_i(x) := a_i(x)·η(x)(ω(x)) and b_i(x) := B·Θ_i(x)^ℝ. Then:
   - each F_i is a.e. strongly measurable;
   - |F_i| ≤ b_i a.e.;
   - since ∫ Θ dμ < ∞, Θ < ∞ μ-a.e. (ae_lt_top), so (b_i(x))_i is summable for a.e. x (ENNReal.summable_toReal);
   - x ↦ Σ'_i b_i(x) is measurable with ∫ ‖Σ'_i b_i‖ₑ d(μ⌞N) ≤ ‖B‖ₑ·∫ Θ dμ < ∞, hence integrable;
   - where Θ(x) < ∞, (a_i(x)) is summable (|a_i(x)| = Θ_i(x)^ℝ), so HasSum (i ↦ F_i(x)) (m(x)·η(x)(ω(x))).
   The dominated convergence theorem for series (hasSum_integral_of_dominated_convergence) gives HasSum (i ↦ ∫_N F_i dμ) (∫_N m·η(ω) dμ).
7. (Identification of the terms.) Fix i. By 3(b), for μ-a.e. x ∈ M_i, θ_i(x)·ξ_i(x)(ω(x)) = θ_i(x)·s_i(x)·η(x)(ω(x)). So R_i.action(ω) = ∫_{M_i} θ_i·ξ_i(ω) dμ = ∫_{M_i} s_i·θ_i·η(ω) dμ (setIntegral_congr_ae). Since M_i ⊆ N, this equals ∫_{N ∩ M_i} s_i·θ_i·η(ω) dμ = ∫_N 1_{M_i}·s_i·θ_i·η(ω) dμ (setIntegral_indicator) = ∫_N F_i dμ.
8. By steps 5–7, HasSum (i ↦ R_i.action(ω)) (R'.action(ω)) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). ∎

Each term equals R_i.action(ω) because ξ_i = s_iη a.e. on M_i; hence HasSum (R_i.action ω) (R'.action ω).
